papers.title: Random coloured digraphs defined by a Markov logic network
papers.abstract: A Markov Logic Network (MLN) $M$ is a probabilistic relational model used in Statistical Relational Artificial Intelligence for defining a probability distribution $P_D^M$ on the set $W_D$ of possible worlds with domain $D$ for an arbitrary finite domain $D$. An MLN consists of first-order formulas, which we call soft constraints, with associated weights which are nonnegative real numbers. The behaviour of the probability distribution, including the effect of the weights, on different domain sizes is poorly understood. We approach the problem in a systematic way by studying sequences $(P_n^M(\psi) : n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots)$ where $\psi$ is a first-order sentence and $P_n^M(\psi)$ is the probability that $\psi$ holds in $W_D$ where $D = [n] := \{1, \ldots, n\}$. We consider a first-order language that can express a property $P(x)$ and relation $R(x, y)$ and show that all of the following cases can be realized for an MLN $M$ such that each of its soft constraints is a boolean combination of $P(x)$, $P(y)$ and $R(x, y)$ in which both $x$ and $y$ appears: For every first-order sentence $\psi$, $P_n^M(\psi)$ converges to 0 or 1 as $n\to\infty$. For every first-order sentence $\psi$, $P_n^M(\psi)$ converges as $n\to\infty$ but not necessarily to 0 or 1. There is a first-order sentence $\psi$ such that $P_n^M(\psi)$ does not converge as $n\to\infty$. In fact, all three cases can be realized even after fixing the soft constraints and, for any $\varepsilon > 0$, by varying their weights by less than $\varepsilon$. We also show that, given any MLN as described above, we can efficiently determine which case it belongs to by inspecting the MLN. Then we show that if the weights are scaled by $1/n$ then we end up in case~(1) no matter how the weights are chosen.

papers.title: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.

papers.title: Computational trust as intuitionistic knowledge
papers.abstract: In this paper, we will argue that the notion of computational trust can be understood as a form of fallible intuitionistic knowledge grounded in verification. This approach naturally captures a key aspect of trust: it involves vulnerability. Specifically, it validates the principle that verification leads to trust but does not validate the opposite principle that trust leads to verification. Thus, we can trust on good grounds that some program will perform according to its specification but the program might still fail. We present a simple logic for capturing this notion of computational trust based on constructive modal propositional logic extended with a trust modality, which will be specified in an inferential fashion and by utilizing the proofs-as-programs correspondence.

papers.title: Invariance and Expressiveness: Modal Variations
papers.abstract: This contribution focuses on bisimulation invariance as the hallmark of modal model theory and of modal modelling. It exemplifies traditional as well as more recent ramifications \&\ extensions of classical results -- involving variant modes of bisimulation equivalence and matching modalities also beyond plain Kripke structures, and emphasising especially the technical challenges in finite model theory and other non-elementary settings. Main results to be discussed revolve about the theme of expressive completeness phenomena: beside expressive completeness under bisimulation invariance in relation to first-order background logics, in the style of van Benthem--Rosen characterisations, this also concerns maximality results under criteria form abstract model theory, in the style of Lindstroem theorems.

papers.title: A translation of Maehara's "Eine Darstellung der Intuitionistischen Logik in der Klassischen"
papers.abstract: A key motivation for Heyting's intuitionistic logic was to gain a formal notion of Brouwer's idea of mathematics as a "construction of the mind". One might thus argue that Heyting's Calculus should also correspond to a notion of provability. Inspired by this idea, G\"odel formalised this connection via an embedding into a modal calculus, which is now known as the modal logic S4. While in his original publication, he only proved soundness for the embedding from intuitionistic propositional logic into S4, the converse was proved fifteen years later by McKinsey and Tarski. Although, it was later discovered that G\"odel also had obtained a proof of the faithfulness of his embedding in unpublished notes in 1941. Rasioa and Sikorski later extended G\"odel's embedding to first-order intuitionistic logic. In 1954, Maehara independently obtained the same results using proof-theoretic methods, even extending the embedding to one from intuitionistic first-order logic into intuitionistic first-order modal logic. This document presents a faithful English translation of Maehara's 1954 paper.

papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $\Gamma_0$
papers.abstract: What does a recursive definition mean in a grounded logic, where a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? This paper takes Kripke's answer for truth, the least fixed point, as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term; Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, making each an inductive definition. IGA is omega-sound and proof-grounded: sound and complete for a semantics whose certificates are its own proofs. IGA proves Goodstein's theorem, the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, and, along Gentzen's route, the consistency of Peano Arithmetic. IGA certifies the Veblen notation below every $\varphi(n,0)$: its accessibility ordinal there is $\varphi(\omega,0)$, that of the paracomplete truth theory PKF. Every theorem is machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL; order types and PKF's ordinal are cited. IGA proves the Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for it, which it does not, and that bivalence is sound exactly when the order is well-founded. So $\Gamma_0$ lies exactly one instance of excluded middle away, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in an internal form of Kleene's $\mathcal{O}$ are interderivable over IGA. Bivalence at the Bachmann-Howard order keeps proof-groundedness. One such claim buys well-foundedness of the countable part of Buchholz's notation at every finite level, of type $\psi_0(\Omega_\omega)$, and $k$ stratified bivalence rules give a proof-grounded system proving the countable part up to level $k$ well-founded; $k$ iterated closings-off of truth do too, sound only for a closed-off model. Unrestricted conditional proof is inconsistent (Curry's paradox); the purchase is implication at a hypothesis not provably decided.

papers.title: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.

papers.title: Rigidity of ordinal spaces
papers.abstract: A Hausdorff space $Y$ is called rigid if, for every positive integer $k$, every continuous open $k$-to-one map $p:X\to Y$ from a Hausdorff space $X$ admits a partition of $X$ into $k$ open sets, each mapped homeomorphically onto $Y$. We show that the Sorgenfrey plane is not rigid, giving negative answers in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ to Velichko's questions on finite products of rigid spaces and on strongly zero-dimensional spaces. For ordinal spaces, we prove in $\mathsf{ZF}$ that every regular uncountable cardinal with the tree property is rigid. In $\mathsf{ZFC}$, we obtain a characterization for arbitrary limit ordinals: a limit ordinal $\alpha$ is rigid if and only if every coherent family $\langle f_\xi:\xi<\alpha\rangle$, where $f_\xi:\xi\to\{0,1\}$, admits a uniformization. As a consequence, a limit ordinal is rigid if and only if its cofinality is rigid. The characterization also implies that $\omega_1$ is not rigid in $\mathsf{ZFC}$, answering a question of Velichko.

papers.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over a quadratic field
papers.abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic field $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{25}\in K$.

papers.title: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

papers.title: The Order of the Non-universal Tree of a Hilbert Space with Respect to the Haar Basis
papers.abstract: In his 1994 doctoral thesis, Bossard introduced the notion of the non-universal tree $T_{NU}(X)$ associated with each separable Banach space $X$ which does not contain an isomorphic copy of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Together with the order operation defined on well-founded trees, we obtain a method of classifying the complexity of separable Banach spaces by the degree of isomorphism of finite-dimensional subspaces of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Despite further refinement of this concept in later years, we are unaware of any specific instances of direct exhibitions of the order of the non-universal tree for a concrete space and basis. We show that if $H$ is any separable Hilbert space, then $o(T_{NU}(H)) = {\omega} + 1$ when taken with respect to the Haar basis for $C(2^\mathbb{N})$, demonstrating that the class of Hilbert spaces is the least complex class with respect to this measurement when considering this basis.

papers.title: Property B: A Baumgartner-style Property that Applies to Preservation of $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_2$ under Iterations with Supports of Size $\aleph_1$
papers.abstract: We prove a theorem on iterated forcing that can be used for preservation of $\aleph_2$ and $\aleph_1$ in the usual iterations along an ordinal, with supports of size $\aleph_1$ of forcings that have amalgamation properties similar to those present in the perfect set forcing. The work is modelled after Baumgartner's Axiom A and his proof that iterations with countable support of the same preserve $\aleph_1$. In honour of James E. Baumgartner, the property introduced here is called Property B$(\kappa)$. The known additional difficulties when forcing at cardinals higher than $\aleph_1$ make for a less general theorem and a more complex theorem on the iteration, which is not an iteration theorem in the classical sense. The results extend to other cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\kappa^{<\kappa}=\kappa$, in place of $\aleph_1$. We give examples of individual forcings that have Property B$(\kappa)$ and their products. In particular, we introduce a correct version of the generalised perfect set forcing, which we call Perfect Set Forcing with Respect to a Filter. We give its basic properties and show that for the right kind of filter $\mathcal F$ this kind of forcing is iterable with supports of size $\le\kappa$. Our further work has extended some of the results from the paper to iterations along any well-founded partial order.

papers.title: Comments on Choiceless Chain Conditions
papers.abstract: In [11] it was suggested that the countable chain condition should be defined in the absence of choice as "every predense set contains a countable predense subset". During his tutorial at the "120 Years of Choice" conference in 2024, Philipp Schlicht remarked that this definition does not have an iteration theorem in $\mathsf{ZF}$. We provide a proof of this claim. Specifically, we show that if every finite support iteration of ccc forcings is again ccc, then the Axiom of Choice for countable families of countable sets must hold. However, we prove that under the assumption of the Principle of Dependent Choice, the finite support iteration of ccc forcings is again ccc. This requires correcting some issues with the definition of properness (and therefore Mekler's definition of ccc) from [1]. We then study Knaster principles and their relations to this version of ccc.

papers.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Diophantine subset of $\mathbb{Q}$. More precisely, there exist an integer $m\ge 1$ and a polynomial of total degree at most four in $m+1$ variables whose rational zero set projects onto $\mathbb{Z}$ under the first coordinate. We construct a Diophantine model of $\mathbb{Z}$ on an elliptic curve and use it to define real intervals with rational endpoints, each containing an integer. A denominator bound identifies a rational number in a sufficiently short interval with that integer. The key ingredients are a criterion for square denominators, obtained using the Tian--Yuan--Zhang genus-point criterion for congruent number elliptic curves, and a height bound from quaternionic abelian surfaces. The Green--Tao theorem supplies prime progressions needed to define squaring, and hence multiplication, in the model. Our proof is inspired by OpenAI's approach to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$, but does not rely on the $2$-converse or $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and invoked by OpenAI.
